questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The walkable and bike-friendly infrastructure of the Netherlands
English being a widely spoken language
The fact that it was within the European Union

Additional comments:

questions.answer: Very easy

questions.answer: Mail correspondances

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was possible to live in a dorm

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets. There was an available common kitchen with a stove.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Remember to apply for university housing early to get a good placement on the waiting list. Living in a dorm on a campus is a great opportunity to make friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You did it online. There was a section on the university website where all the deadlines were visible. Before you could register for courses, it was possible to see an overview of all available courses, however, the schedules weren't released beforehand meaning that you couldn't know for sure if the courses you had applied for pre-approval for would be possible to take simultaneously.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mail correspondance, office hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got into the minor that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep in mind that some courses might overlap as you usually have 2 courses simultaneously.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a part of a minor which is an introduction to the master of the same name. The course level was 300 described as: "Advanced level course (entry requirement of level 100 or 200) Characteristics: textbooks not specifically intended for educational purposes; independent study of the examination material; students are able to apply their knowledge to new problems in examination situations."

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. The communication and formality was the same. There was  a larger amount of written assignments compared to at home.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AB_1047 Experimental Cell Biology I
AB_1048 Experimental Cell Biology II
AB_1052 Metabolomics
AB_1291 From Protein to Cell
AB_470610 Molecular Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Molecular Microbiology. It is slightly time-intensive, but you learn a lot, and the course is overall well-structured

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying common appliances and basic furniture. Renting a bike.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were less expensive compared to at home, public transport was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The local gym is cheap and, depending on where you live, very easy to access.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty of events were  planned by RA's on-campus. There were also  creative spaces available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a gym, visit the creative space, see some stand-up.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See local cities. Bike around in the area. Travel to nearby countries such as Germany or Brussels (it's pretty cheap by bus).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The environment was very international, and we didn't get that many opportunities to make Dutch friends. I did manage to invite some people from uni over at one point.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to interact with people at uni, go to bars or other social areas.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Dutch people can seem reserved, and it is generally easier to make international friends who don't already have a social sphere.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The direct-ness, the informality of students and teachers. The general non-competitiveness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for housing early. Housing can be expensive.
There aren't that many biomedical minors available for SCIENCE students. However, it is still possible to assemble your own schedule with individual courses.
The grade-system is very different. Don't be disappointed if you don't get top-grades as they are rarely given out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Show up for the events that are planned in the first months and keep an open mind. While you can get by without Dutch, it does help to learn some basic words as a lot of public areas have signs written in Dutch.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was easy to stay in ones comfort zone and only hang out with your dorm/friends. Looking back, I  wish I'd taken more solo-trips and explored other cities some more.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
